findings.title: Unresolved findings escape the gate: stage_id relabelling and dropped findings are not detected
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:278 evaluates the terminal-state rule only for findings whose stage_id === the gate's stage; rules.mjs:275-277 only cross-checks finding IDs listed by the gate's final PASS records; stages.json review_rounds[].records and the <role>.findings.json sidecars of earlier (FAIL) rounds are never consulted; tools/gates/import-findings.mjs:42-51 imports sidecar findings without checking f.stage_id against --stage. Scenario A: round-1 code-security FAIL raises F-DG0-1xx (High, mandatory, OPEN); its stage_id is set (or imported) as 'DG1' -> validate.mjs --stage DG0 PASSes with the finding still OPEN. Scenario B: the OPEN finding is simply never imported / removed from findings.json; the round-2 PASS records do not list it -> the gate PASSes. Reproduction script (static, not executed - Bash unavailable in this run): docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/repro.test.mjs tests R1a and R1b.
findings.expected: Every finding raised in any review round of the stage (all review_rounds records and their findings sidecars) must exist in findings.json with stage_id equal to the stage and be in a terminal state with independent verification; a finding cannot be deferred to another stage by relabelling without an explicit, audited transfer.
findings.actual: A High mandatory-violation finding raised at DG0 can remain OPEN (relabelled stage_id) or be absent from findings.json and validate.mjs --stage DG0 still exits 0, bypassing the 'zero unresolved Critical/High and mandatory findings' gate condition.

findings.title: Invocation provenance is satisfied by a fabricated 4-field meta.json; transcript and result are never checked
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:225-235 (checkInvocation) reads only runs/<stage>/<run_id>/meta.json and checks role, invocation_reference.session_id, exit_code and is_error. It does not require transcript.jsonl.gz or result.json to exist, does not compare meta.result_session_id (written by run-agent.sh:77) to the requested session, does not bind the record's 'assignment' to meta.assignment/assignment_sha256, does not check meta.task/stage or that the run started after candidate.frozen_at, and run-agent.sh:66-89 records no hash of the transcript. The validator's own fixture (tools/gates/tests/validator.test.mjs:60-67) proves a hand-written {run_id, role, invocation_reference:{session_id}, exit_code:0, is_error:false} passes. Scenario: anyone with repo write access (Bash is unguarded for every role) writes docs/delivery/runs/DG0/DG0-x/meta.json for each role plus four PASS review records and a gate record -> validate.mjs --stage DG0 and --pipeline (historical) exit 0 with no agent ever invoked. Historical mode (rules.mjs:341-395) re-reads these mutable, candidate-excluded files from the working tree, so approvals can also be rewritten after the fact. Repro: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/repro.test.mjs R0 (not executed in this run).
findings.expected: The validator refuses a review/audit/verification unless the referenced run has transcript.jsonl.gz and result.json present, meta records a SHA-256 of the transcript that matches, the transcript's init/result lines carry the same session_id, result_session_id equals the requested session_id, the run's assignment path/SHA matches the record's assignment file, meta.stage equals the gate stage, and the run started after the candidate froze.
findings.actual: Provenance (DG0 approval condition 'required stage agents actually invoked', A23/A24) can be satisfied entirely with fabricated metadata; the check does not raise the cost of forgery beyond writing one small JSON file.
findings.fix_summary: Fixed in 51f5b9cf40790f54016e8b363959279eda1bfaab (round-7 repair); regression tests in tools/gates/tests/validator.test.mjs

verification.note: Round 7 kept this OPEN only because of the empty-transcript gap (F-DG0-132), and that gap is now closed. Expected behaviour from the finding, checked on d6626258: transcript.jsonl.gz and result.json must exist (rules.mjs:281-284); their hashes must match meta (283-284); the transcript must carry an init line and a final successful result for the session, unconditionally (296-319); result_session_id must equal the session (277); the assignment path and SHA-256 must bind the record, meta and the transcript-bound prompt (310-313, 321-323); meta.stage must match (275); and the run must start after the freeze, from a commit containing the manifest (324-332). Reproduction R8-06 builds the original r1 R0 shape (hand-written meta, no transcript and no result). It is rejected on d6626258 with 'missing transcript.jsonl.gz', 'missing result.json', 'transcript is empty' and 'no init line'. The empty-transcript forgery that reopened this finding (R8-01/03/04/05) is rejected too, and both still reproduce on e11b5f08 (02-repro-r8-on-e11b5f0.log). What remains is forging a complete, internally consistent run directory, including a transcript with plausible Write calls. That is the residual D-021 discloses, and it needs repository write access: an accepted limit of a repository-local validator, not this defect.

findings.title: The frozen manifest's spec is not bound to stages.json candidate_spec or to the D-005 exclusion policy
findings.reproduction: rules.mjs:315-331 recomputes the candidate using manifest.spec, read from docs/delivery/candidates/<DGx>.manifest.json (itself candidate-excluded metadata). Nothing checks manifest.spec against stages.json candidate_spec, and nothing restricts exclude globs to the D-005 set (trading_agent/** + META_EXCLUDES). stages.json candidate_spec is also excluded metadata, so changing it never changes any candidate. Scenario: a manifest frozen with spec.exclude ['src/**'] (or 'apps/**') -> later edits and new files under src/ never change the recomputed ID and validate.mjs --stage keeps PASSing. Repro: repro.test.mjs R3 (not executed in this run).
findings.expected: The validator requires manifest.spec to equal the stage's candidate_spec and rejects exclude patterns beyond the approved policy (or requires a decision record for each), so exclusions cannot silently hide deliverables.
findings.actual: Arbitrary exclusions in the manifest are accepted; the only safeguard is a human reviewer noticing the spec.

findings.title: Write guard: protected list omits Claude configuration surfaces and trading_agent/, and paths are checked lexically (symlinks followed)
findings.reproduction: (1) tools/agents/write-scopes.json:3-17 protects .claude/settings.json but not .claude/settings.local.json, .mcp.json, .claude/hooks/** or .claude/commands/**, and does not protect trading_agent/** (CLAUDE.md: 'Do not modify it'; also excluded from every candidate, so edits there are invisible to gates). An implementer (allow '**') may Write .claude/settings.local.json, which Claude Code loads into every later project session, including guarded agent runs; per Claude Code settings documentation a 'disableAllHooks': true there would disable the PreToolUse guard for all later runs (not reproduced end-to-end: running claude is out of scope for this review). (2) guard-write.mjs:52-54 resolves the target lexically with path.resolve and never calls realpath, so a Write to docs/analysis/lnk/lib/rules.mjs, where docs/analysis/lnk -> ../../tools/gates, is ALLOWED for transformation-analyst while it lands in tools/gates. (3) Matching is case-sensitive: on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS/Windows) 'Tools/Gates/x' bypasses the deny list. Policy context: Bash is not path-guarded for any role (all ten definitions include Bash); this is disclosed in agent-protocol.md:75, agents.md:69 and D-009, and the compensating control is the orchestrator's git status check. Repro: repro.test.mjs R6 (not executed in this run).
findings.expected: Deny list includes .claude/** (except none), .mcp.json and trading_agent/** for implementers; the guard canonicalises the target with fs.realpathSync on the deepest existing ancestor and denies if either the lexical or the real path is protected; comparisons are case-folded on case-insensitive platforms.
findings.actual: Implementers can write Claude configuration that governs later guarded sessions and the unrelated user project; symlinked paths bypass deny rules.

findings.title: Runner hygiene: unvalidated --stage/--task/--role, second-resolution run IDs can overwrite evidence
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/run-agent.sh:17-39: STAGE, TASK and ROLE are used unvalidated in filesystem paths (OUT=runs/$STAGE/$RUN_ID; a --stage containing '../' writes evidence outside runs/) and in RUN_ID, which may then not match the schema pattern ^DG[0-7]-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$. RUN_ID has one-second resolution and 'mkdir -p' reuses an existing directory, so two runs of the same role/task started in the same second overwrite each other's transcript/meta. No shell injection found: all values are quoted and passed to python via argv with a quoted heredoc; the prompt is a single argument.
findings.expected: Validate --stage against ^DG[0-7]$ and --task/--role against a safe charset; include the session UUID (or a mkdir without -p that fails on existence) in the run directory.
findings.actual: Evidence directories can collide or be misplaced by argument mistakes.

findings.reproduction: .github/workflows/delivery-gates.yml:18 'actions/checkout@v4' and :21 'actions/setup-node@v4' resolve to whatever the tag points to at run time; a moved tag changes the code that runs the gate job. Otherwise the workflow is sound: permissions contents: read, fetch-depth: 0 for historical checks, no secrets referenced, and every step's non-zero exit fails the job.
findings.expected: Third-party actions pinned by full commit SHA (with the tag in a comment).
findings.actual: Tag-pinned actions.

findings.title: Gate validator accepts a review whose invocation_reference points at an unrelated run of the same role (e.g. the T-DG0-LOAD load check)
findings.reproduction: QA_REPO_ROOT=<repo> node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative.test.mjs --test-name-pattern QA-N27. The fixture builds a valid DG0 gate, then adds a second, successful qa-verifier run whose meta.json has task T-DG0-LOAD, assignment docs/delivery/assignments/DG0/T-DG0-LOAD.md and started_at before the candidate froze. It then points the qa-verifier review record's invocation_reference at that run. validateGate() returns no errors. In the real repository, successful LOAD runs exist for all four review roles (docs/delivery/runs/DG0/DG0-T-DG0-LOAD-{domain-reviewer,code-security-reviewer,qa-verifier,release-auditor}-*), so a complete DG0 gate could validate with no review invocation ever having run. checkInvocation() in tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs compares only role, session_id and exit status.
findings.expected: The validator (A24: rejects missing or invalid evidence; A23: separate actual review evidence) rejects a review or audit record whose run is not bound to it: the run's meta.assignment/task must match the record's assignment/review task, and the run must start after the candidate froze (meta.started_at >= stage candidate.frozen_at, or meta.head_commit_at_start containing the frozen commit). A regression test must cover this.
findings.actual: The validator accepts the record. validateGate returns [] (test QA-N27 fails with 'validator accepted an invalid gate (no errors)'). The meta.json fields that would bind a run to a review (task, assignment, assignment_sha256, started_at, head_commit_at_start) are recorded but never checked.

findings.title: Finding closure is taken from orchestrator-written findings.json; the reviewer's own verification sidecar, the verification evidence and the fix revision are never checked
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:408-418 accepts CLOSED_VERIFIED/REJECTED_INVALID when findings.json carries a verification object with result PASS, by_role != owner and a valid run. collectRaisedFindings (rules.mjs:342-367; filename filter at :360) never reads <role>.verifications.json, so the reviewer-authored verification is not the source of truth. verification.evidence paths and fix_revision (rules.mjs:416 only checks truthiness) are not checked. Reproduced with GATE_TOOLS=/tmp/dg0-sec-r2 node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-2/repro-r2.test.mjs: (N1b) on a fully valid gate, add round-2/code-security-reviewer.verifications.json {finding_id F-DG0-101, result FAIL, status_after OPEN} while findings.json says CLOSED_VERIFIED/PASS citing that reviewer's round-2 run. validateGate returns []. (N1c) Set fix_revision 'not-a-commit' and verification.evidence ['does/not/exist.log']. validateGate returns []. Precondition: whoever maintains findings.json (the orchestrator, D-008) writes the verification object directly instead of via import-findings.mjs. The reporter's final-round record can still be PASS, because nothing ties a PASS verdict to the absence of a FAIL verification.
findings.expected: A finding reaches CLOSED_VERIFIED/REJECTED_INVALID only if a reviewer-authored verifications sidecar in a round of this stage contains an entry for that finding with result PASS and a matching status_after. The sidecar belongs to a PASS or FAIL record whose run is bound (assignment and post-freeze, as for reviews). findings.json.verification must equal that entry. Verification evidence must be existing repository files, and fix_revision must be a commit that is an ancestor of the candidate's source_commit. A FAIL entry in a later round supersedes an earlier PASS.
findings.actual: The gate's 'zero unresolved Critical/High and mandatory findings' condition can be met by editing one object in findings.json, even when the reporting reviewer explicitly recorded the fix as FAIL.

findings.title: Write guard: an implementer can plant a nested '.git' (tools/.git, docs/.git, .github/.git) that moves the guard's repo root and un-protects gate rules, sources and delivery records
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/guard-write.mjs:40-48 (repoRootOf) takes the nearest ancestor containing '.git' as the repository root, and :72 matches patterns against the path relative to that root. solution-architect/frontend/backend/kpi/devops have allow '**'. 'tools/.git', 'docs/.git' and '.github/.git' match no deny pattern, so a Write to them is allowed. After Write tools/.git ('gitdir: /nonexistent'), a Write to tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs is evaluated as 'gates/lib/rules.mjs' and ALLOWED. The same holds for tools/agents/write-scopes.json (via tools/.git), docs/delivery/stages.json and docs/source/playbook.md (via docs/.git), and .github/workflows/delivery-gates.yml (via .github/.git). Reproduced through decide() and end-to-end through the hook entry point (exit 0): repro-r2 test N3. The planted file is invisible in 'git status' (09-nested-git-visibility.log), so it persists silently for later sessions. Edits to tracked protected files still show as ' M' and change the candidate, so the orchestrator's git-status check and the candidate hash remain compensating controls. Bash remains unguarded (disclosed, D-009/D-020); this finding is about the Write-tool guard itself.
findings.expected: The guard uses a fixed repository root (for example the root of the tree containing tools/agents/guard-write.mjs, or `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` evaluated once by the hook) rather than the nearest '.git'. It also denies writes of any path segment named '.git' (the pattern '**/.git' and '**/.git/**') for every role.
findings.actual: Implementer roles can disable the write guard for protected paths with two Write calls, and the first one leaves no trace in git status.

findings.title: Candidate identity omits the entry type and the file mode: a file containing 'symlink:<t>' collides with a symlink to <t>, and chmod +x/-x does not change the candidate
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/candidate.mjs:58-60 hashes a symlink as sha256('symlink:'+target). candidateId (:117-124) serialises only '<sha256>  <path>', dropping entry.type, so a regular file whose bytes are 'symlink:app.txt' hashes identically to a symlink -> app.txt (repro-r2 N4). The git mode (100644 vs 100755) is not hashed either, so removing the executable bit from tools/source/check_extraction.sh (which CI runs directly) or tools/agents/run-agent.sh leaves the candidate unchanged (repro-r2 N5).
findings.expected: The canonical line includes the type and the mode, e.g. '<sha256>  <mode>  <path>', with mode taken from git (100644/100755/120000) in both manifestFromRef and manifestFromWorkingTree.
findings.actual: Two distinct deliverables share one candidate ID; a behaviour-changing mode change is invisible to A25 change detection. Exploitation of the collision requires crafting a file whose content equals the link's marker string; impact is low. I would accept this as a Low observation.

findings.title: Working-tree candidate depends on the platform's line-ending conversion; no .gitattributes pins it
findings.reproduction: manifestFromWorkingTree (tools/gates/lib/candidate.mjs:73-96) hashes on-disk bytes, while manifestFromRef hashes blobs. With core.autocrlf=true (the Git for Windows default), checked-out text files contain CRLF, so candidate.mjs --stage and validate.mjs --stage (current mode) compute a different ID from the frozen one (repro-r2 N6). The repository has no .gitattributes, and D-005 is silent on line endings. The effect is fail-closed (a false 'changed' result, not a bypass).
findings.expected: Either a committed .gitattributes ('* -text' or '* text=auto eol=lf') makes checkouts byte-identical to blobs on every platform, or current mode hashes the git-normalised content (git hash-object --path / the clean filter). D-005 states the rule.
findings.actual: Candidate identity is not platform-independent in current mode; a Windows reviewer or CI runner cannot reproduce the frozen ID.

findings.title: A finding's verification may cite any successful run of the verifying role, including a pre-freeze load-check run; the F-DG0-201 binding is not applied to verifications
findings.reproduction: QA_REPO_ROOT=<frozen worktree @83860be> node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r2.test.mjs --test-name-pattern QA2-N11. The disposable fixture builds a fully valid DG0 gate in which F-DG0-201 (Medium, mandatory) was raised by qa-verifier in round 1 and is CLOSED_VERIFIED in round 2. The test then adds a successful qa-verifier run for task T-DG0-LOAD (assignment docs/delivery/assignments/DG0/T-DG0-LOAD.md, started 11:00Z, before the 13:00Z freeze) and points findings.json F-DG0-201.verification.invocation_reference at it. validateGate() returns []. Cause: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:417 calls checkInvocation(repo, stageId, v.invocation_reference, v.by_role, errors, ...) without a binding argument, so the assignment/assignment_sha256 and notBefore checks at rules.mjs:302-308 are skipped for verifications. In this repository, successful LOAD runs exist for all four review roles (docs/delivery/runs/DG0/DG0-T-DG0-LOAD-*), so any finding in the stage could be closed with a verification that cites a run which never examined the fix. docs/delivery/agents.md line 32 (D-016) states the opposite: 'The validator refuses any review, audit or finding verification unless its run ... executed exactly the cited assignment, started after the candidate froze'.
findings.expected: A CLOSED_VERIFIED or REJECTED_INVALID finding's verification must be bound to a run that could have verified it. The run must start after the fix (at least after fix_revision was committed, or after the candidate the fix is in froze). It must have executed a review or verification assignment of this stage, for example the verifier's round-N assignment, whose record lists the finding in its <role>.verifications.json. A regression test must cover the pre-freeze LOAD-run case. Otherwise agents.md/D-016 must be corrected, but the gate condition 'independent verification' then remains unenforced.
findings.actual: validateGate returns no errors (test QA2-N11 fails with 'validator accepted an invalid gate (no errors)'). The round-2 re-verification of F-DG0-201 itself passed only for reviews (QA2-R201, QA2-R201b pass); the same defect class remains open for finding verifications.

verification.note: Reproduced on 83860be (QA2-N11: a closure citing the verifier's pre-freeze LOAD run is accepted). findings.reproduction: QA2-N14 in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r2.test.mjs runs 'chmod +x app/main.txt' on a validated fixture. findings.title: Reviewer-authored records and sidecars are not bound to the reviewer's run, and 'append-only' covers deletions only: editing them in place drops findings, flips FAIL verifications and FAIL verdicts
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:537-543 (checkReviewRounds) scans git history only with --diff-filter=D, so a committed file under reviews/<DGx>/ or runs/<DGx>/ may be MODIFIED in any later commit. Nothing binds the content of a review record (checkReview, rules.mjs:315-341), a findings sidecar (collectRaisedFindings, rules.mjs:345-370) or a verifications sidecar (collectVerifications, rules.mjs:454-481) to the run that supposedly wrote it: checkInvocation (rules.mjs:265-312) only proves that SOME successful run of that role exists. tools/agents/run-agent.sh:109-118 records no manifest of the files the agent wrote. Historical immutability (rules.mjs:586-626) starts only at the first commit where the gate record is APPROVED, and it pins whatever the files contained at that moment. Reproduced with GATE_TOOLS=/tmp/dg0-sec-r3 node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-3/repro-r3.test.mjs (log 02-repro-r3-candidate.log): (a) test 4: round 1 raised High mandatory F-DG0-101, and the round-1 files were committed. A later commit rewrites round-1/code-security-reviewer.findings.json to {findings:[]}, sets the round-1 record's findings to [] and removes the entry from findings.json. validateGate current, validateGate historical (after approval) and validatePipeline all return []. (b) test 5: the reviewer's committed round-2 verifications sidecar says FAIL/OPEN. A later commit edits it to PASS/CLOSED_VERIFIED and mirrors findings.json. validateGate returns []. (c) test 6: a committed qa-verifier record with verdict FAIL and a FAIL check is edited to PASS. validateGate returns []. The real runs show a mechanical check is feasible: the transcripts contain the reviewer's Write/Bash tool calls. No file under reviews/DG0 or runs/DG0 has been modified or deleted in the real history so far (git log --diff-filter=D/M empty), so a stricter rule would not block DG0.
findings.expected: Once written by the reviewer's run, reviewer artefacts cannot be changed without the validator noticing. Minimum: (1) the history check rejects modifications as well as deletions (--diff-filter=DM, or first-committed blob == current blob) for every file under reviews/<DGx>/**, runs/<DGx>/** and the round's assignment, and it also compares the working tree with the first committed version. (2) The runner records the SHA-256 of every file the run created or changed (git status before/after) in meta.json, which is itself hash-bound. The validator requires every review record, findings sidecar and verifications sidecar to match the outputs of the run that its record cites. (3) The orchestrator commits the run's outputs together with its run directory immediately after the run, and D-016/D-018 describe the residual window. The error message 'review evidence is append-only' must be true.
findings.actual: The fixes for F-DG0-101/F-DG0-110 moved the source of truth from orchestrator-written findings.json to reviewer sidecars, but the sidecars and records can be edited by the same actor at the same cost (one JSON edit). An unresolved High finding can be removed, a reviewer's FAIL verification turned into a closure, or a FAIL review turned into PASS, and the gate, historical mode and pipeline still pass. D-018 states the evidence is append-only, but the implementation only forbids deletion.

findings.title: Working-tree candidate mode is read from the filesystem exec bit, so it disagrees with git where core.fileMode=false (Windows default); the result fails closed
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/candidate.mjs:92 derives the mode of a working-tree file from st.mode & 0o111. On filesystems without exec bits (NTFS, FAT; git sets core.fileMode=false there), tracked 100755 files (tools/agents/run-agent.sh, tools/source/check_extraction.sh) are hashed as 100644. Then candidate.mjs --stage DGx and validate.mjs --stage DGx (current mode) report a different ID from the frozen one, although git status is clean. repro-r3 test 9 simulates this on Linux: chmod -x plus core.fileMode=false gives an empty git status and a different working-tree candidate. The effect is a false 'changed' result, not a bypass.
findings.expected: For tracked files, the working-tree manifest takes the mode from the index (git ls-files --stage, which manifestFromWorkingTree already runs at :74) when core.fileMode is false, or always. Only content is read from disk.
findings.actual: Current-mode candidate identity is not reproducible on Windows checkouts. The F-DG0-113 line-ending fix works, but the F-DG0-112 mode fix reintroduces a platform dependency. I would accept this as a Low observation.

findings.title: Write-once working-tree check is blind to skip-worktree/assume-unchanged index flags (local validation only)
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:593 (checkWriteOnce) detects uncommitted edits to committed evidence only through 'git status --porcelain'. The validator then reads the working-tree bytes (checkInvocation output binding, rules.mjs:310-318; collectVerifications). If a committed file is flagged with 'git update-index --skip-worktree' (or --assume-unchanged), git status stays empty while the file on disk differs. repro-r4.test.mjs test 13 ('BYPASS N2'): a committed round-2 FAIL/OPEN verification sidecar, its run's meta.json and findings.json are flagged skip-worktree. They are then edited on disk to PASS/CLOSED_VERIFIED, with meta.outputs re-pointed. 'git status --porcelain' is empty, and validateGate(repo,'DG0') returns [] (05-repro-r4-candidate.log). Impact is limited to a local working tree: CI checks out committed content, and committing the forgery shows up as an 'M' in history. But the release-auditor decides the gate by running validate.mjs locally.
findings.expected: The write-once check refuses to run (or reports an error) when any file under the write-once paths carries the skip-worktree or assume-unchanged flag. For example, 'git ls-files -v -- <paths>' must show no 'S' or lower-case tags. Alternatively, it compares working-tree bytes with the HEAD blob directly (hash each file and compare with 'git ls-tree HEAD').
findings.actual: A locally tampered working tree passes validate.mjs --stage DG0 with a clean git status. I would accept this as a Low observation if the orchestrator documents that the gate decision is re-validated from a clean checkout (CI), or adds the ls-files -v check.

findings.title: Run output binding records end-of-window bytes at any path a file tool was merely attempted on; 'exact bytes your run wrote with its file tools' is not what is checked
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/run-agent.sh:163-179 adds every Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit tool_use file_path from the transcript to written_by_tools, without looking at the matching tool_result, so hook-denied and failed calls count too. meta.outputs (run-agent.sh:160) is the post-snapshot hash taken when the run ends. The validator (rules.mjs:310-318) accepts a file when it equals meta.outputs and its path is in written_by_tools. So bytes produced by any other writer during the run window are bound as the reviewer's own: a Bash command, or a concurrent process such as the orchestrator's session. End-to-end with the real runner and a stub claude in a disposable clone (06-runner-e2e.log, FAKE_MODE=denied): the agent's Write of the review record is denied (tool_result is_error=true). Another writer puts 'B written by someone else' there during the window. meta.written_by_tools lists the record, meta.outputs holds sha256(B), and the runner auto-commits B as 'review evidence'. Real history shows the same gap in benign form (12-transcript-write-content.log): my own round-3 findings sidecar differs from the content of the run's Write call, because the same run later edited it with sed. The binding cannot tell the difference. The stream-json transcript does carry the full Write content and the tool_result status, so a stricter check is feasible.
findings.expected: Either (a) the runner counts only tool calls whose tool_result is not an error, and for Write records sha256(last successful Write content) per path. The validator, or the runner before auto-committing, requires the file to equal that content, and Edit/MultiEdit reconstruction is either done or those paths are flagged. Or (b) D-021 and agent-protocol.md ('the validator binds each of them to the exact bytes your run wrote with its file tools') are corrected to say what is actually bound: the bytes present at the end of the run window at paths the agent targeted with a file tool. The residual, overwrites by other writers during the window, is then disclosed next to the existing self-hashing residual.
findings.actual: The binding holds any end-of-window bytes at attempted paths. The documentation overstates it. The incremental risk is below the already disclosed residual (a fully fabricated run directory), so the severity is Low. It is not acceptable as an observation until the documentation matches the mechanism.

findings.title: Runner auto-commit passes reviewer-written paths as unquoted git pathspecs: glob characters commit unrelated files, and failures are masked by '|| true'
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/run-agent.sh:205-211 runs git add/commit with an unquoted $(cat "$OUT/../.commit-list-$RUN_ID"). Each written path is word-split by the shell and interpreted by git as a pathspec with glob magic. In a disposable clone with a stub claude (06-runner-e2e.log, FAKE_MODE=glob), the agent Writes a file literally named 'docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-9/x*'. An unrelated tracked file 'xy.md' in the same directory was modified by someone else during the window. The auto-commit 'run: <id> (review evidence ...)' contains 'A .../x*' and also 'M .../xy.md', which the agent never wrote. That turns another party's change into write-once 'review evidence' attributed to the run. By code inspection (not executed): a path containing whitespace is split into two pathspecs, 'git add' fails, and under set -e the runner then aborts before 'exit "$EXIT"' with the evidence uncommitted. The '|| true' on the commit (run-agent.sh:210) also hides every commit failure (hook, identity, lock), so the write-once window never starts, and neither meta.json nor the exit status records that.
findings.expected: Build the pathspec list safely: NUL-separated, 'git add --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul' with ':(literal)' magic or GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1. Commit exactly those paths. Treat 'nothing to commit' as the only tolerated non-zero result, and otherwise fail the runner with a distinct exit code and a message, so the orchestrator notices that the evidence was not committed.
findings.actual: Unrelated modified files can be swept into a reviewer's auto-commit, and commit failures are silent.

findings.title: Committed Python bytecode caches (tools/agents/**/__pycache__/*.pyc) are part of the frozen candidate; running the candidate's own runner-metadata tests rewrites them, so tools/gates/prefreeze.sh DG0 exits 1 on a fresh checkout and the candidate ID drifts
findings.reproduction: 1) git worktree add <tmp>/wt a059b55a7024f68cc7e33fedc8bd023d3b091336 (or git clone + checkout). 2) node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG0 prints sha256:c13a4f8e…3ff68 (matches the freeze). 3) Run tools/gates/prefreeze.sh DG0 (or only `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/agents/tests -p 'test_*.py'`, which CI and prefreeze both run). Every check prints PASS, then 'FAIL  uncommitted candidate changes: M tools/agents/__pycache__/run_meta.cpython-311.pyc, M tools/agents/tests/__pycache__/test_run_meta.cpython-311.pyc', exit 1. 4) node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG0 now prints a different ID: sha256:e4008b07…7190e in the worktree, sha256:1d672b48…bbf33 in a fresh clone. Cause: commit d2630de (round-5 repair) added the two .pyc files. The frozen manifest lists them (c13a4f8e93cad95a.manifest.json lines 243 and 313), and the repo has no .gitignore. A CPython 3.11 .pyc header records the source mtime (here 1790608540 = 2026-09-28T15:15:40Z, the orchestrator's tree), and the code object embeds the absolute source path. Any other checkout has a different mtime and path, so importing run_meta.py recompiles and rewrites the cached files with checkout-specific bytes (13675 → 13740 bytes in the worktree).
findings.expected: The frozen candidate contains only source, with no machine-generated, checkout-specific build artefacts. Running every check the candidate ships (REQ-DLV-023: prefreeze.sh runs the Python unittest suite and then an uncommitted-changes check) passes on any fresh checkout of the candidate, and doesn't change the candidate's content or its recomputed candidate ID.
findings.actual: prefreeze.sh DG0 exits 1 on a fresh checkout of a059b55. It can pass only in the orchestrator's own working tree, where the source mtimes still match the committed caches. After the CI or prefreeze Python tests run, the working tree no longer hashes to the frozen candidate ID, and the drifted ID differs between checkouts. A reviewer who runs the required tests in the repository tree (rather than a disposable copy) would silently desynchronise the candidate. Fix: git rm --cached both .pyc files, add a .gitignore for __pycache__/ and *.pyc (or run the tests with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 / -B in prefreeze and CI), and exclude such paths from the candidate manifest. Then re-freeze. I rate it Medium and mandatory: it is limited in scope and trivial to fix, but it breaks candidate reproducibility and makes a required DG0 check fail on the candidate.

findings.title: Committed Python bytecode (__pycache__/*.pyc) makes the candidate non-reproducible: the candidate's own checks rewrite it on any clean checkout, so prefreeze.sh fails, --freeze refuses and the working-tree candidate ID drifts
findings.reproduction: The candidate (a059b55) tracks tools/agents/__pycache__/run_meta.cpython-311.pyc and tools/agents/tests/__pycache__/test_run_meta.cpython-311.pyc (manifest entries), and the repository has no .gitignore. CPython reuses a .pyc only if the source mtime and size in its header match the file on disk. The headers carry the orchestrator's mtimes (run_meta.py: 2026-09-28T15:15:40Z). In any fresh checkout the source mtime is the checkout time, so importing the module rewrites both files. The candidate's own documented checks do exactly that: prefreeze.sh:19 and .github/workflows/delivery-gates.yml:30-31 both run 'python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/agents/tests', which imports run_meta. Steps (03-pyc-prefreeze-fresh.log): (1) git worktree add of a059b55: status clean, candidate.mjs --stage DG0 prints sha256:c13a4f8e...ff68. (2) tools/gates/prefreeze.sh DG0: every check PASSes, then 'FAIL uncommitted candidate changes: M tools/agents/__pycache__/run_meta.cpython-311.pyc, M .../test_run_meta.cpython-311.pyc', exit 1. (3) candidate.mjs --stage DG0 now prints sha256:657843aa...; in a second worktree it printed sha256:ac1a2d5d... (01-existing-tests.log run), so the value depends on checkout time. (4) validate.mjs --stage DG0 in current mode recomputes from the working tree (rules.mjs:689-691), and --reconcile (rules.mjs:860) reports the tree as differing and every review as STALE. (5) candidate.mjs --stage DG0 --freeze refuses: 'uncommitted candidate changes ... changed: [both .pyc]' (16-prefreeze-dirty-gap.log, part A). With a Python other than 3.11 (CI's ubuntu-24.04 ships 3.12), new untracked cpython-312.pyc files appear instead, and they too enter the working-tree candidate (candidate.mjs:90 lists untracked, non-ignored files). The main tree passes only because its .pyc headers happen to match its own mtimes (04-prefreeze-main-tree.log). The committed bytecode is also opaque to review, and it embeds the orchestrator's absolute path (/home/user/My-owns/...). I checked that it is currently code-equal to the committed sources (05-pyc-equivalence.log), so this is not hidden code.
findings.expected: Candidate identity is deterministic and platform-independent (D-005): a clean checkout of the frozen commit reproduces the candidate ID before and after the candidate's own documented checks, and the pre-freeze check passes on a clean checkout. Build artefacts are not deliverables. Fix: remove the __pycache__ files from the repository and add a .gitignore with '__pycache__/' and '*.pyc' (ignored files are excluded from the working-tree candidate by --exclude-standard). Also export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 in prefreeze.sh and in the CI job.
findings.actual: Two build artefacts are part of the frozen deliverable. On any machine other than the one that compiled them, the documented checks rewrite them. prefreeze.sh DG0 then exits 1, --freeze refuses, current-mode gate validation and reconcile see a different candidate, and the ID depends on checkout time. It fails closed, so no gate can be passed wrongly, but independent verifiers (reviewers or auditor in clean clones) cannot reproduce the pre-freeze check or the candidate after running the tests.

findings.title: An empty (or newline-only) transcript.jsonl.gz skips every transcript check: init line, D-022 replayed prompt, final result and the D-021 transcript replay are all bypassed
findings.reproduction:
tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:281-314 (checkInvocation, candidate e11b5f08): lines = gunzip(transcript).split('
').filter(Boolean). The init-line check (295-297), the D-022 CLI-replayed prompt check (300-309) and the successful-result check (310-312) all sit inside 'if (lines.length) { ... }' (294). The D-021 independent replay of the run's Write/Edit calls (341-345) is also guarded by 'if (lines.length && ...)'. A transcript that is valid gzip of '' or of '


' gives lines = [], so none of these checks runs and no error is pushed. The only transcript requirement left is that its SHA-256 equals meta.transcript_sha256, and the forger writes that field. Reproduction (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-7/repro-r7.test.mjs, log 01-repro-r7-on-e11b5f0.log), all against the e11b5f08 validator. Control 2: a transcript of unparsable lines is rejected ('no init line'). Tests 3/4: replacing a reviewer's transcript with gzip('') or gzip('


') and re-hashing it in meta gives validateGate(...) === []. Test 5: a qa-verifier record is rewritten after its run and meta.outputs/tool_authored are re-pointed. With the real transcript, the round-7 replay rejects it ('differs from the replay of this run's transcript'). After the transcript is emptied, validateGate returns []. Test 6: the verifying run that closes High F-DG0-101 has an empty transcript and the closure is accepted. Test 7: the same forgery committed and approved passes validateGate(historical). The gap is older than round 7: tests 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 pass on a059b55 as well (02-repro-r7-on-a059b55.log). Scenario: anyone with repo write access (Bash is unguarded for every role) writes docs/delivery/runs/DG0/<id>/{meta.json,result.json,transcript.jsonl.gz(empty)} with self-consistent hashes, the fields checkInvocation reads (role, stage, session, exit_code 0, assignment + sha, started_at after the freeze, head_commit_at_start containing the manifest, outputs/tool_authored hashes), plus PASS records, sidecars and a gate record. They commit it as ordinary new history with current dates, so write-once and back-dating are satisfied. validate.mjs --stage DG0, --historical and --pipeline then exit 0 with no agent ever invoked.
findings.expected: D-016 and D-022 describe the transcript checks as unconditional. A run whose transcript has no init line for the session, no CLI-replayed runner prompt (isReplay: true, carrying run_id and session_id) or no final successful result for the session is rejected. Every bound output must be reconstructible from the transcript's own successful Write/Edit calls. Fix: treat an empty parsed transcript as an error ('transcript is empty'), and run the init, prompt, result and replay checks unconditionally whenever the transcript file exists (a replay result of null must be an error, not skipped). Add regression tests for gzip('') and gzip('\n').
findings.actual: The init, CLI-replayed-prompt, final-result and D-021 replay checks are all skipped for an empty transcript. A fabricated run directory then needs only meta.json, result.json and an empty gzip. That is the same cost as the original F-DG0-102 forgery (one small JSON file plus two trivial files), not the 'complete, internally consistent run directory' that D-021 discloses as the residual. The D-022 and D-021 replay repairs in this round do not hold against it. Mandatory: it lets the gate validator accept invalid provenance evidence (DG0 approval condition: the review protocol and gate validator reject missing/invalid evidence; A23/A24).

findings.title: The CLI-replayed prompt is not cross-checked with meta.assignment / assignment_sha256, so 'executed exactly the cited assignment' rests on unanchored meta fields
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:305-309 require the replayed prompt only to start with "You are invoked as project agent '<role>' for stage <DGx>" and to contain the run_id and session_id. The assignment binding (315-318) compares the record's 'assignment' with meta.assignment and the file's SHA-256 with meta.assignment_sha256. It never compares either with the path and 'sha256 ...' that run-agent.sh:56 writes into the prompt, which is the only assignment statement bound by the transcript hash. Reproduction: repro-r7.test.mjs test 8 (01-repro-r7-on-e11b5f0.log). The replayed prompt of a qa-verifier run is extended with 'Your complete assignment is in the file .../round-9/some-other.md (sha256 000...0)', and validateGate still returns []. The validator's own fixture prompt (validator.test.mjs makeRun) names no assignment at all and passes.
findings.expected: D-016 says a run is accepted only if it 'executed exactly the assignment the record cites (path and SHA-256)'. The validator extracts the assignment path (relative to meta.cwd) and the sha256 from the replayed prompt and requires them to equal meta.assignment / meta.assignment_sha256 (and therefore the record's assignment).
findings.actual: meta.json is not hash-bound by anything, so an edited or fabricated meta can re-point a genuine transcript at a different assignment. Impact is limited: committed meta.json files are write-once, and fabricating a new run directory is the disclosed D-021 residual. I would accept this as a Low observation once F-DG0-132 is fixed.

findings.title: The write-guard hook selects which guard to run from the hook's cwd (git rev-parse --show-toplevel), so in the documented '--cwd <worktree>' mode (and after a Bash cd into any nested repo) Write/Edit to the main repository's protected paths are allowed
findings.reproduction: Every tools/agents/settings/<role>.settings.json:9 runs g="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tools/agents/guard-write.mjs"; node "$g" <role>. The guard found this way pins GUARD_ROOT to its own location (guard-write.mjs:42) and allows any path outside that root as 'scratch' (guard-write.mjs:80). run-agent.sh:108/117 start claude with 'cd "$CWD"' and --settings from the main repository (run-agent.sh:40), and agents.md:96 / D-004 prescribe '--cwd <worktree>' for concurrent writers. (1) Worktree mode, file tools only, no Bash: see 09-guard-worktree-cwd.log. A 'git worktree add' of the candidate is created, then the real hook command is run with cwd = worktree and a Write payload for the MAIN checkout. For backend-workflow-engineer, transformation-analyst and code-security-reviewer, tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs, docs/delivery/stages.json, .claude/settings.local.json, docs/delivery/gates/DG1.json and tools/agents/write-scopes.json all return rc=0 (allowed). The same payloads from cwd = main checkout return rc=2 (blocked). (2) Live confirmation that Claude Code runs the PreToolUse hook in the session's current cwd: see 08-hookcwd-live-probe.log. After a Bash 'cd' into a nested git repo whose tools/agents/guard-write.mjs only logs, an in-scope Write in this very session executed that nested file (hook_process_cwd = the nested repo), not the real guard. So an agent can also replace the guard by planting any guard-write.mjs in a nested repo and cd-ing into it. With an unmodified guard copy in the nested repo, every main-repo path is allowed (07-guard-nogit-and-nested-cwd.log B1).
findings.expected: REQ-DLV-007's procedure and agents.md:28 / D-020 say the guard 'fix[es] the guarded root to this repository', so a nested .git 'can't move the root'. In every supported run mode, including '--cwd <worktree>', Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit to the orchestrator repository's protected paths must be blocked for implementers and reviewers. Fix sketch: the hook command should invoke a fixed guard path, for example the absolute path of the main repository's tools/agents/guard-write.mjs, written into the settings by run-agent.sh so it does not depend on the hook's cwd. That guard must protect both REPO_ROOT and the run's worktree (or treat any path inside any checkout of this repository as guarded), rather than allowing everything outside its own root. Add a regression test that runs the hook entry point from a worktree and from a nested repository.
findings.actual: The guard in force is whichever guard-write.mjs sits at the git toplevel of the hook's cwd. In the sanctioned worktree mode, that guard protects only the worktree, and the main repository (gate rules, agent definitions, Claude configuration, stages.json, gate records) is writable through plain file tools. Mitigations: the orchestrator's git-status check and full-candidate review would surface committed changes. But REQ-DLV-007 makes the mechanical file-tool guard the control, and the git-status check is documented only as the compensating control for Bash. The Bash-cd variant needs a Bash step, which is already disclosed as unguarded. The worktree variant needs none. Every recorded DG0 run so far used cwd = the repository root (12-run-cwds.log), so the worktree variant has not been exercised. It is, however, the mode D-004 prescribes for concurrent writers from P1 onward. I did not audit past transcripts for the Bash-cd variant.

verification.note: Fixed in c24ec04 (in candidate 85a0efa, sha256:1e959f25...0c54). Hook selection no longer depends on the hook's cwd. Every role's settings and frontmatter hook now runs $MTH_GUARD_ROOT/tools/agents/guard-write.mjs, and fails closed with exit 2 when MTH_GUARD_ROOT is unset. run-agent.sh:102 exports MTH_GUARD_ROOT=$REPO_ROOT, and the agent's Bash can't change the parent process environment. guard-write.mjs:44 takes GUARD_ROOT from it, and guardedRoots() adds every 'git worktree list' entry, with the deepest root winning. Differential reproduction with my own script (repro-r10-guard.sh), which runs the real hook commands. OLD cbc755d, section A: all 15 writes from cwd = worktree into the main repository's protected paths (rules.mjs, stages.json, .claude/settings.local.json, gates/DG1.json, write-scopes.json; roles backend-workflow-engineer, transformation-analyst, code-security-reviewer) return rc=0, ALLOWED. In-scope controls return rc=0. The live runner probe (05-live..., control run) confirms that the hook blocks under the real runner. The regression tests in guard.test.mjs (both F-DG0-134 tests) pass: 56/56 node tests. The defect reported here, the guard being chosen from the hook's cwd so that worktree mode left the main repository unguarded, is fully fixed. The fix introduced a separate fail-open path: on git errors, worktrees drop out of the guarded roots, where the old hook failed closed. findings.title: The gate validator cannot load its own schemas when the repository path contains a space or non-ASCII characters (rules.mjs uses URL.pathname, which stays percent-encoded), so the F-DG0-223 portability goal is still not met end to end
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs line 37: `const here = new URL(".", import.meta.url).pathname;` then schema() reads join(here, "..", "schemas", ...). URL.pathname keeps percent-encoding (node -e: new URL('.', 'file:///a%20b/x.mjs').pathname -> '/a%20b/'), unlike fileURLToPath, which candidate.mjs, validate.mjs, import-findings.mjs and guard-write.mjs use. Clone cbc755d into '<tmp>/qa9 space dir/My Projects/repo' or '<tmp>/qa9-مستخدم/repo' and run `node tools/gates/validate.mjs --pipeline` (or --reconcile, or --stage DG0): uncaught ENOENT on '.../qa9%20space%20dir/My%20Projects/repo/tools/gates/schemas/stages.schema.json', exit 1. `node --test tools/gates/tests/*.test.mjs tools/agents/tests/*.test.mjs` there: 36 of 53 fail (including the new 'F-DG0-223: a genuine prompt binds when the checkout path contains spaces'), and `tools/gates/prefreeze.sh DG0` exits 1. The same clone at a path without spaces passes everything. Automated: QA_REPO_ROOT=<candidate clone> node --test --test-name-pattern=QA9-F224 docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r9.test.mjs -> not ok (exit 1). findings.title: Regression from the F-DG0-134 fix: guardedRoots() swallows git errors, so when 'git worktree list' fails the worktrees drop out of the guarded roots and their protected paths become writable. An agent can trigger the failure with one Write to ~/.gitconfig, which the guard allows as scratch
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/guard-write.mjs:47-54: guardedRoots() runs 'git -C <root> worktree list --porcelain' inside try { } catch { /* git unavailable: the root itself is still guarded */ }. On any git error, only MTH_GUARD_ROOT stays guarded. decideOne() (guard-write.mjs:98-99) then returns allow ('outside the guarded repository (scratch)') for every path inside a worktree that lies outside the main root. The documented concurrent-writer mode (D-004, run-agent.sh --cwd <worktree>) always uses such a worktree. Reproduction: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-10/repro-r10-guard.sh. It runs each role's REAL hook command from tools/agents/settings/<role>.settings.json via sh -c, with cwd = the worktree and MTH_GUARD_ROOT = the main clone, as run-agent.sh:102 exports it. Section F sets HOME to a fake home whose .gitconfig is malformed ('[core' plus a garbage line), which makes 'git worktree list' exit 128. That is exactly what an agent's Write to $HOME/.gitconfig produces, and section E shows the guard allows that Write (rc=0, scratch). Results on the new candidate 85a0efa (04-guard-repro-new-85a0efa.log, section F), all rc=0 (ALLOWED) for backend-workflow-engineer: <worktree>/tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs, <worktree>/docs/source/playbook.md, <worktree>/.claude/settings.local.json, <worktree>/tools/agents/write-scopes.json, and the relative path tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs. Controls: the same targets with a well-formed .gitconfig give rc=2 (blocked), and the main-repo path gives rc=2 even with the malformed config. Section G shows git missing from PATH has the same effect: worktree path rc=0. On the OLD commit cbc755d (03-guard-repro-old-cbc755d.log, sections F and G), the same conditions gave rc=2 ('write guard missing'). The old hook located the guard with git rev-parse and failed CLOSED on any git error. So the fix turned a fail-closed path into a fail-open one. No regression test exercises guardedRoots() with git failing (08-static-residuals-and-cleanup.log).
findings.expected: The guard fails closed. If the set of guarded roots can't be determined (git missing, git erroring, unparsable output), every write is blocked, or at least every write outside the agent's known scratch areas. A worktree of the repository must never be reclassified as scratch because a tool call failed. Suggested fix: in guardedRoots(), on error, throw or return a sentinel that makes decide() block with 'cannot determine guarded roots'. Also consider having the runner pass the run's worktree (its --cwd) explicitly, for example as MTH_GUARD_EXTRA_ROOTS, so protection does not depend on git at hook time. Add a regression test that runs the hook with a malformed global git config (HOME or GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL override) and with git absent from PATH, and expects exit 2 for worktree paths.
findings.actual: Any agent that can make git fail inside the hook process turns off protection of its own worktree's gate rules, agent tooling, Claude configuration and source documents: tools/gates/**, tools/agents/**, .claude/**, docs/source/**. The trigger is one file-tool Write outside the repository, for example $HOME/.gitconfig, which the guard allows. Because git would also be broken for the agent's own Bash commands, the agent could restore the file with a second Write after the protected writes. Mitigations: the protected-path changes land in the worktree, not the main repository, and would appear in the diff the orchestrator integrates and in the full-candidate reviews. This is the same compensating control as for F-DG0-134, which was classified Medium and mandatory, and this finding is classified the same way for consistency. At DG0, no run has used worktree mode yet.

findings.title: The runner loads user-level Claude settings ($HOME/.claude/settings.json), which the write guard treats as writable scratch. A {"disableAllHooks": true} there switches off the write guard for every later agent run, and the git-status compensating control can't see the change
findings.reproduction: run-agent.sh:112-115 and 121-124 start 'claude -p --agent <role> ... --settings <role>.settings.json' without '--setting-sources' and without an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so user settings load in every run. The CLI (2.1.283) honours disableAllHooks from user settings; its bundle contains 'hooks are turned off in your settings (disableAllHooks)'. The guard classifies every path outside the repository and its worktrees as scratch (guard-write.mjs:98-99; write-scopes.json $comment). So a Write to $HOME/.claude/settings.json is allowed for every role: 04-guard-repro-new-85a0efa.log section E, rc=0 for backend-workflow-engineer and code-security-reviewer. LIVE reproduction with the real runner (05-live-user-settings-disable-hooks.log). Disposable clone at 85a0efa; role transformation-analyst; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointing at a throwaway directory, so the real home config was never touched. (1) Control, empty user settings: the Write to tools/gates/PROBE-ctl.txt was BLOCKED by the write guard. (2) User settings pre-seeded with {"disableAllHooks": true}, which is what an earlier run's allowed scratch Write leaves behind: the Write to tools/gates/PROBE-att.txt SUCCEEDED ('File created successfully'), and the file exists with content 'probe-att'. (3) Same-session attempt: the agent's Write of {"disableAllHooks": true} to the user settings file was refused only by the auto-mode permission classifier ('[Self-Modification]'), not by the write guard. The next Write, to tools/gates/PROBE-self.txt, was then blocked by the guard. An untested variant: an 'env' entry in user settings could redirect MTH_GUARD_ROOT to an agent-planted guard.
findings.expected: REQ-DLV-007 / D-020: file-tool writes outside a role's scope are mechanically blocked, and every Claude configuration surface that can disable or redirect the guard is protected, not only the in-repository ones (.claude/**, .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md). The runner should not let configuration outside its control weaken the guard. Suggested fix: run agents with '--setting-sources project' (or project,local, both protected) and/or a runner-owned, per-run CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Add the user-config paths ($HOME/.claude/**, $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/**, $HOME/.claude.json, and $HOME/.gitconfig / $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/** for F-DG0-135) to a deny list that applies outside the guarded roots. Disclose the residual in D-020/D-023. Add a live or harness regression test showing a pre-seeded user disableAllHooks no longer disables the guard.
findings.actual: One allowed Write to $HOME/.claude/settings.json, or one Bash command, which is unguarded by design, disables the write guard for every subsequent run on the machine: implementers and reviewers alike, main repository and worktrees. The disclosed compensating control for unguarded writes is the orchestrator's 'git status' after every run (D-020; agent-protocol 'Write scopes'). It cannot detect this, because the file is outside the repository, and nothing in run meta records it (the snapshot covers repository files only, run-agent.sh:79-96). In my live same-session attempt, the permission classifier happened to refuse the settings Write. That is a probabilistic control, not the mechanical guard REQ-DLV-007 requires, and the guard itself allowed it. Protected-path changes made in a later unguarded run would still show up in git status and in full-candidate review. That limits the impact to Medium, not High.

findings.title: One shell command persistently and invisibly disables the write guard for every later run: {"disableAllHooks": true} in .claude/settings.local.json, a setting source the runner still loads, hidden through .git/info/exclude or ~/.config/git/ignore. Neither git status nor the runner's snapshot or config_snapshot sees it
findings.reproduction: run-agent.sh:126 and :135 start every agent with '--setting-sources project,local', so the 'local' source (.claude/settings.local.json in the working directory's project) is still loaded. D-024 relies on 'Project and local settings are protected in-repository paths', but that protection covers only file tools. Bash is unguarded by design (D-009/D-020/D-024), and its compensating controls are the orchestrator's 'git status' and, since D-024, the runner's config_snapshot and external_config_changed. An ignore rule defeats both. (a) config_snapshot() (run-agent.sh:80-88) hashes 8 fixed files plus the regular files in .git/hooks. It does not include .git/info/exclude, the worktrees' info/exclude, the global excludes file (core.excludesFile, default ~/.config/git/ignore), or the project's .claude/settings.local.json / CLAUDE.local.md. (b) snapshot() (run-agent.sh:91-96) lists files with 'git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard', which omits ignored files. (c) 'git status' omits ignored files. LIVE reproduction with the real candidate runner and CLI 2.1.283, in a disposable clone of 7e99163 plus a probe-assignment commit (11-live-local-settings-exclude.log). Step 1 simulates an earlier agent's single Bash command: printf ".claude/settings.local.json\n" >> .git/info/exclude && printf '{"disableAllHooks": true}' > .claude/settings.local.json. Afterwards 'git status --porcelain' is EMPTY. Step 2 is a later, ordinary transformation-analyst run through tools/agents/run-agent.sh, asked to Write tools/gates/PROBE-loc.txt. Result: 'File created successfully', the file exists with content probe-loc, and meta.external_config_changed = []. Control on the same runner and commit without step 1: the identical Write is BLOCKED by the write guard (04-live-user-settings-new-7e99163.log). Variant (12-global-ignore-variant.log): the same two files hidden through ~/.config/git/ignore are invisible to config_snapshot, git status and the runner snapshot. Harness 06-config-snapshot-harness.log, step f: an .git/info/exclude change is NOT DETECTED.
findings.expected: REQ-DLV-007 / D-024: a Claude configuration surface that can switch off the guard must not be loaded unless the runner's controls can see it. Suggested fix, any of: (1) start agents with '--setting-sources project' only, because nothing legitimate needs local settings; (2) before and after each run, fail closed (for example exit 71) if an untracked or ignored .claude/settings.local.json, CLAUDE.local.md or .mcp.json exists at any depth in REPO_ROOT or in the run's --cwd, found with 'git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard' over the protected globs; (3) add .git/info/exclude, .git/worktrees/*/info/exclude and the resolved core.excludesFile (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore or ~/.config/git/ignore) to config_snapshot, and snapshot ignored files under protected paths. Narrow D-024's wording, and add a regression test: a planted, ignored local settings file makes the runner refuse to run or flags external_config_changed.
findings.actual: A single Bash command in any run, by any role, switches the write guard off for all later runs of every role. It is invisible to both compensating controls: git status is clean, meta.external_config_changed is empty, and meta.outputs lists only the later protected write, not its cause. The same mechanism can hide a planted CLAUDE.local.md, which would inject instructions into later agents. I did not test that one live. Mitigations, which is why this is Medium and not High: the trigger is a protocol-violating Bash command; the protected writes that later runs make are still visible in git status ('?? tools/gates/PROBE-loc.txt' in the probe) and in full-candidate review; and at DG0 no implementer run has happened since the fix. This is the same class and classification as F-DG0-136, which was Medium and mandatory. F-DG0-136's reported vector, user-level settings, is fixed (see its verification); this is a different, in-repository vector that the D-024 controls do not cover.

findings.title: The config_snapshot tamper check misses symlinked git hooks, and the review-evidence auto-commit runs hooks. A symlinked pre-commit hook runs after the post-run snapshot and can add extra files, for example tools/gates/*, to the 'run: ... review evidence' commit. Other surfaces are also unmonitored
findings.reproduction: run-agent.sh:87 lists hooks with 'find "$REPO_ROOT/.git/hooks" -type f', which skips symlinks. The auto-commit at run-agent.sh:169-180 runs 'git commit' without --no-verify or '-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null'. Harness 06-config-snapshot-harness.log, extracting config_snapshot() and the diff step verbatim from 7e99163: a regular .git/hooks/pre-commit is DETECTED (step d), but a pre-commit SYMLINK to a script outside the repository is NOT DETECTED (step e), and git then runs it on commit ('YES: SYMLINKED-HOOK-RAN'). 07-hook-smuggle.log reproduces the runner's exact add and commit sequence (GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, --pathspec-from-file, --pathspec-file-nul, one run directory in the list). A pre-commit hook that runs 'git add tools/gates/rules.mjs' puts that file in the auto-commit next to the run's meta.json. Also not monitored (06 steps g and h): ~/.claude.json (user MCP servers), ~/.claude/agents/**, and $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, because the snapshot is hard-wired to $HOME/.claude. And rules.mjs:278-279 ignores a present but non-array external_config_changed value, because only Array.isArray values are checked.
findings.expected: D-024 states that the runner detects changes to .git/hooks and refuses to auto-commit, so that no code runs during the auto-commit. The hook listing should include symlinks, hashing the link and its target (for example 'find -type f -o -type l'). The auto-commit should run hooks off ('git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit --no-verify') and check that the commit's file list equals the pathspec list. The snapshot should honour CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and include ~/.claude.json. The validator should reject a non-array external_config_changed.
findings.actual: An agent that has already misused Bash can run code in the runner's context at auto-commit time, undetected by external_config_changed. That code can put extra changes into a commit labelled as review evidence. This is Low, and not a mandatory violation, because it needs the disclosed, unguarded Bash channel, which could also commit directly during the session. The smuggled change is still visible in the commit diff, and 'git status' still showed 'MM' for the file in my reproduction. The validator's candidate recomputation and prefreeze's working-tree check would also flag candidate drift. I would accept this as an observation if D-024's detection claim is narrowed to what the snapshot actually covers. The fix is small.

findings.title: D-024 detection gap: a shell-planted .claude/settings.local.json with disableAllHooks switches the write guard off for later runs (loaded via --setting-sources project,local), and hiding it with .git/info/exclude, or planting it in a worktree working directory, leaves no trace in the run evidence
findings.reproduction: 1) Live, real CLI 2.1.283 in a disposable clone of candidate 7e99163, with the runner's own flags (MTH_GUARD_ROOT=<clone>; claude -p --settings <clone>/tools/agents/settings/qa-verifier.settings.json --setting-sources project,local): asked to Write <clone>/docs/source/QA11-LIVE-*.txt. Control run: 'BLOCKED by write guard ... (protected path)', no file. With <clone>/.claude/settings.local.json = {"disableAllHooks": true}, no guard hook runs, and 'File created successfully' writes the protected docs/source file (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-11/05-live-local-settings-disable-guard.log). 2) Runner end to end (run-agent.sh from the candidate, stub `claude` on PATH doing what an agent's unguarded Bash could do), in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r11.test.mjs: QA11-R4 (control), a plain shell write of .claude/settings.local.json, shows in meta.outputs and in git status. QA11-R5: `echo .claude/settings.local.json >> .git/info/exclude` and then the same write gives runner exit 0, external_config_changed [], the file absent from meta.outputs, and `git status` empty. QA11-R6: the same file written into the agent's worktree --cwd gives runner exit 0, external_config_changed [] and nothing in meta.outputs; only that worktree's own git status shows it. config_snapshot() (run-agent.sh) covers ~/.claude/settings*.json, git config files, managed settings, .git/config, .git/info/attributes and .git/hooks, but not .git/info/exclude and not in-repository or worktree Claude local configuration. snapshot() uses `git ls-files --exclude-standard`, so .git/info/exclude blinds it.
findings.expected: D-024 and docs/delivery/agents.md say the runner starts agents with --setting-sources project,local so settings can't switch the guard off, that project and local settings are protected in-repository paths, and that the runner detects configuration changes outside the candidate (exit 71; validator rejects the run). A loaded configuration surface that can disable the guard should therefore be either (a) not loaded, e.g. `--setting-sources project`, since project settings are tracked so tampering shows in git status, or (b) covered by the tamper detection: snapshot <REPO_ROOT>/.claude/settings.local.json, CLAUDE.local.md and .mcp.json, the same files under the run's --cwd and every worktree, and .git/info/exclude, including ignored files for these paths, so exit 71 fires. Add a runner-level regression test like QA11-R5/R6.
findings.actual: Under the runner's exact flags, the guard can be disabled persistently for all subsequent agent runs (any role) by one Bash command in an earlier run. With the .git/info/exclude variant, or when planted in a worktree working directory, this leaves no trace in meta.json (outputs, external_config_changed), the runner exits 0 and auto-commits, and the main repository's `git status` is clean. The remaining control is the auditor's transcript review, where the Bash command would be visible. The Write/Edit enforcement itself is intact, and 'Bash is not path-guarded' is a disclosed residual (D-009/D-020/D-024). That's why I rate this Medium and non-mandatory rather than High: the defect is that D-024's detection claim does not cover the one loaded surface that defeats the guard. Scope note: my live check used --permission-mode acceptEdits and the haiku model to keep it cheap. Hook execution happens before permission evaluation and doesn't depend on the model, but I did not repeat it under --permission-mode auto.

findings.title: OS Bash sandbox escape (D-025): an agent plants a NEW top-level module (e.g. json.py, uuid.py) in the writable repository root; the runner's own unsandboxed 'python3 -c' / 'python3 -' helpers import it from cwd (sys.path[0]==''), executing attacker code OUTSIDE the sandbox as the runner/orchestrator. It can write any protected path (tools/gates, .git/hooks, review records) and forge gate approvals.
findings.reproduction: The D-025 sandbox generated by tools/agents/agent_settings.py denies COMMON_DENY paths but NOT the repository root itself, and deny_except() (agent_settings.py:148-170) denies only EXISTING entries, so NEW top-level files are writable. Confirmed live in my own reviewer sandbox: creating /home/user/My-owns/zz-sec-writable-probe.tmp succeeded (rc=0), and my run's settings.json denyWrite contains neither the repo root nor 'json.py'. run-agent.sh runs its helper Python with the ambient (repository-root) cwd, NOT inside the 'cd "$CWD"' subshell, and several helpers use 'python3 -' / 'python3 -c' whose sys.path[0]=='' (verified: python3 -c 'import sys;print(repr(sys.path[0]))' -> ''): classifier_outage (run-agent.sh:64, 'python3 -', imports json) runs after each agent turn; CONFIG_CHANGED (run-agent.sh:167, 'python3 -c', imports json) and the auto-commit helpers (run-agent.sh:182,198, 'python3 -', import json/subprocess) run at the tail of every reviewer run; the session-id helper (run-agent.sh:46, 'python3 -c') runs at the START of the next run. A json.py placed at the repo root by an agent is therefore imported by the unsandboxed runner. LIVE end-to-end in a disposable clone of the candidate commit (repro-r12-cwd-python-shadow.sh -> 01-cwd-python-shadow.log): a code-security-reviewer run plants json.py at the root; the runner's post-run Python imports it and the payload runs OUTSIDE the sandbox, writing tools/gates/PWNED-by-json-shadow.txt (a sandbox-denied path) and a .git/hooks/pre-commit hook. The log shows imports with argv=['-c'] and argv=['-'] (the classifier_outage and CONFIG_CHANGED helpers). STEALTH variant (repro-r12-cwd-python-shadow-stealth.sh -> 02-cwd-python-shadow-stealth.log): the payload self-deletes json.py and defers its write until after the runner's post-run config_snapshot. Result: meta.external_config_changed == [], meta.bash_sandbox == true, 'git status --porcelain' is EMPTY, the review evidence is auto-committed, and the attacker code then runs on the orchestrator's next ordinary 'git commit' (hook-ran.txt == HOOK-RAN-OUTSIDE-SANDBOX) with no trace in the run evidence.
findings.expected: Per docs/delivery/threat-model.md ('Mechanically prevented': an agent writing a protected path with the shell is blocked by the OS Bash sandbox, which has 'no unsandboxed escape'), no shell action by a sandboxed agent may cause code to run outside the sandbox or write a protected path. Concretely: the runner must not import cwd-relative modules. Run every helper with 'python3 -P' (or PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 / 'python3 -I' / 'python3 -S'), or run the helpers from a fixed non-repository directory, or use only absolute script files (run_meta.py-style) instead of 'python3 -c' / 'python3 -'. The sandbox deny list should also deny creation of new top-level files that shadow stdlib modules in any directory a runner helper executes from (or the helpers should never execute from an agent-writable cwd). Add a regression test: a planted repo-root json.py/uuid.py must not be imported by run-agent.sh's helpers.
findings.actual: A single ordinary, sandbox-permitted Bash write (creating a new file at the repository root, which the sandbox allows) lets an untrusted agent execute arbitrary code as the runner/orchestrator, entirely outside the OS sandbox that D-025 introduced this round as the primary mechanical control. The escaped code can rewrite tools/gates (the validator), forge or alter review/gate records and findings.json, plant persistent git hooks, or disable the write guard for later runs. This is a privilege escalation across the core trust boundary (untrusted agent -> trusted orchestrator identity). The stealth variant evades all three compensating detections (config_snapshot/external_config_changed, git status, and the auto-commit file-list check) and leaves no trace in the run evidence. This is not a disclosed residual: threat-model.md residual #1 concerns a party able to write the repository OUTSIDE any sandbox; here the sandboxed agent itself escapes, which the model asserts is prevented.

findings.title: D-025 sandbox escape without a trace: an analyst or implementer shell can plant gitignored Python bytecode (e.g. docs/analysis/tools/csv.pyc) that the orchestrator's unsandboxed tools/gates/prefreeze.sh then imports and executes, writing protected paths (.git/hooks, tools/gates, HOME configuration) while git status, the run snapshots, config_snapshot and the candidate all stay clean
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone of candidate 7f09967 (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-12/07-pyc-shadow-prefreeze.log). 1) agent_settings.build() for transformation-analyst and backend-workflow-engineer does not deny docs/analysis/tools/csv.pyc: the analyst's confined area and every implementer's area include docs/analysis. 2) Compile a small csv.py whose payload writes a file and then hands over to the real csv module, into docs/analysis/tools/csv.pyc as sourceless bytecode. .gitignore line 4 (*.py[cod]) ignores it, so `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` is empty. The runner's snapshot (`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`) doesn't list it, and the working-tree candidate ID is unchanged (sha256:21f142b8…). 3) `tools/gates/prefreeze.sh DG0` runs `python3 docs/analysis/tools/check_counts.py`. The script directory comes first on sys.path, so `import csv` loads the planted bytecode. Variant A writes tools/gates/QA12-PYC-MARKER.txt, and prefreeze's final candidate check catches it. Variant B writes .git/hooks/post-commit, which is outside the candidate: prefreeze prints PASS on all nine checks and exits 0, the hook file exists, and git status and the candidate ID are unchanged. 4) Runner end to end, with a stub `claude` performing the plant as a transformation-analyst run (QA12-P1 in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r12.test.mjs): the runner exits 0, external_config_changed is [], the pyc is not in meta.outputs, and git status shows only the run directory. QA12-P2 shows prefreeze executing the planted bytecode and exiting 0.
findings.expected: threat-model.md lists 'An agent writes a protected path with the shell' as mechanically prevented, and 'New untracked files where the sandbox leaves the working directory writable' as detected through git status and the runner snapshots. So an agent-writable file that the orchestrator later executes outside the sandbox should either (a) not be executed from the agent-writable tree: run prefreeze and the analysis checks in a fresh clone of HEAD or inside the same bubblewrap sandbox, and/or use `python3 -I -B` (or PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1) so the script directory isn't searched and bytecode isn't used; or (b) be detected: fail prefreeze and flag the run (exit 71 for confined roles) when `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard` lists any ignored file outside a known cache allow-list, or when *.pyc/__pycache__ appear in the run's snapshot including ignored files. The threat model should also disclose that the orchestrator executes implementer-authored code (tracked or not) outside the sandbox before review.
findings.actual: The plant is invisible to every detection layer. The only trace is the Bash command in the agent's transcript, which the auditor may or may not review. Executed by the orchestrator's documented pre-freeze step, the planted code runs with full orchestrator rights and can write exactly what D-025 denies the agent's shell: git metadata and hooks, gate and agent tooling, Claude configuration. I rate it Medium and non-mandatory, consistent with F-DG0-226. It needs a malicious or prompt-injected analyst or implementer, the file tools and the OS sandbox are intact, and the transcript-review residual still applies. But it is a way around a control the threat model lists as mechanically prevented, not a restatement of a disclosed residual. Related: my own round-7 case QA7-N82 established that ignored __pycache__ doesn't fail prefreeze. That is still correct for the candidate hash, but the same ignore rule makes the bytecode executable without a trace.

verification.note: Original failure reproduced on the round-12 candidate 7f09967 (repro-f229-pyc-plant.sh). I planted gitignored sourceless docs/analysis/tools/csv.pyc and __pycache__/csv.cpython-311.pyc, invisible to git status, with a payload that writes .git/hooks/post-commit and exits 42. QA13-S2: BASH_ENV, NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONPATH and PYTHONSTARTUP don't reach the sandboxed command; BASH_ENV runs once, for sandbox-run.sh itself, in the caller's own environment.
