findings.title: D-037 record-less exemption lets the orchestrator silently delete an imported finding (any status or severity) from findings.json when its raising sidecar has no <role>.json record
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:476 sets recordless=true for a findings sidecar with no <role>.json on disk. rules.mjs:514-521 then skips the 'missing from findings.json (dropped)' error for it. But tools/gates/import-findings.mjs:39-52 imports such a sidecar's findings with or without a record, so the validator can no longer tell 'never imported' from 'imported, then deleted'. Such a finding is listed in no review record, so the independent 'referenced' check (rules.mjs:507-510) is silent too. Reproduced in a disposable --no-local clone of HEAD with a drafted APPROVED gate (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-21/r21-recordless-drop.mjs, log 03-recordless-drop.log). F-DG0-239 is raised only in the record-less round-18 qa-verifier.findings.json and was imported. Deleting it from findings.json gives 0 errors about it (D-037 rules), against 1 'dropped' error with the round-20 rules (a23c4d4). With F-DG0-239 re-statused OPEN, validateGate reports 'unresolved (OPEN)'; deleting it then gives 0 errors. The same path applies to any future interrupted reviewer run that raises a Critical/High finding. Aggravating detail: recordless is taken from the LATEST raising sidecar only (raised.set supersedes, rules.mjs:482). A later record-less sidecar re-listing an earlier, properly raised finding also clears its 'dropped' error (r21-recordless-supersede.mjs, log 01, scenario C). There, only the original record's findings[] listing still catches the drop.
findings.expected: A finding that was ever imported into findings.json can leave it only through a reviewer-verified terminal status. The only tolerated case is a finding that was provably never imported, for example an explicit allowlist such as F-DG0-238, or a git-history check that the id never appeared in findings.json. Simpler still: import F-DG0-238 and let its reporter close it as REJECTED_INVALID (a duplicate of F-DG0-150), so no exemption is needed. If any exemption remains, recordless must hold only when EVERY raising sidecar is record-less.
findings.actual: Deleting an imported, even unresolved, finding raised by a record-less sidecar produces no validator error. The gate rule 'zero unresolved Critical/High findings' can be met by deletion for this class of findings. Before D-037 this was an error.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: withdrew the record-less drop exemption (it could not distinguish never-imported from imported-then-deleted); every sidecar-raised finding must be in findings.json. F-DG0-238 (dup of CLOSED_VERIFIED F-DG0-150) imported for its reporter to close in round 22. collectVerifications still skips record-less verifications. Test in validator.test.mjs.

verification.note: The recordless exemption is removed (rules.mjs:490-496, :527-535). SEC22-6: a finding raised only by a record-less findings sidecar and missing from findings.json is reported '(dropped)'. A record-less verifications sidecar still cannot close anything ('CLOSED_VERIFIED but no reviewer verifications sidecar verifies it'). F-DG0-238 is imported into findings.json (OPEN, qa-verifier), not exempted. The real-repo dry-run reports 0 DROPPED and 0 RECORD-LESS errors. The supersede aggravation noted in the original finding no longer applies to drops. The related immutable-field supersession is raised separately as F-DG0-165 (Low).

findings.title: checkInvocation's D-037 tolerance also accepts a missing, non-hex or fabricated head_commit_at_start, including for gate-round records, not only a 'genuinely pruned' commit
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:393 runs the F-DG0-212 manifest-containment check only if commitPresent(meta.head_commit_at_start). commitPresent returns false for undefined, a non-hex string or any 40-hex id that does not exist, and the branch applies to every binding, including checkReview for gate records. In a disposable clone (r21-commitpresent-probe.mjs, log 04, P3), the real round-20 qa run's meta.head_commit_at_start was set to (c) a non-existent 40-hex, (d) the field removed, and (e) 'not-a-sha'. The head check is now 'accepted' for all three, where the round-20 rules (a23c4d4) rejected all three. A present commit lacking the manifest (b) is still rejected (control). Census (P2): absent heads occur only in rounds 1-12, beyond the shallow boundary; rounds >= 13, including the gate round, have none. Forging meta.json is otherwise within threat-model residual 1, hence Low.
findings.expected: Only a well-formed 40-hex head_commit_at_start that is genuinely unavailable (beyond the shallow boundary or pruned) is tolerated, and only for superseded rounds. For the gate round the commit must be present and contain the manifest. A missing or malformed field is an error.
findings.actual: Missing, malformed or fabricated values skip the check in every round, including the gate round.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: checkInvocation tolerance scoped -- head_commit_at_start must be well-formed 40-hex (missing/null/unknown/HEAD rejected) AND its round genuinely absent (roundSourceCommit unresolved); never gate/retained rounds. Test D-038/F-DG0-159.

verification.note: checkInvocation (rules.mjs:397-410) now rejects a missing, null, 'unknown', 'HEAD', uppercase or short head_commit_at_start, and an absent well-formed head in a retained or gate round (SEC22-5: all rejected; unit test 'D-038 / F-DG0-159' passes). Remaining residue: the 'round absent' predicate itself can be spoofed through a superseded round's manifest source_commit. That residue is tracked in F-DG0-164, not here; the scope stated in this finding (gate round, malformed values) is fixed.

findings.title: The repository is SHALLOW (not 'pruned'), and the validator never detects shallowness: write-once, back-dating and the D-035/D-037 commit tolerances silently depend on clone depth
findings.reproduction: (1) git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository prints true. .git/shallow lists e8361b8 ('DG0 round 12 ...'), whose parent dcb289c is simply not fetched (log 06). D-035 and D-037 (decisions.md rows D-035 and D-037) describe this as a history 'truncated'/'pruned' in an earlier session. The commits are outside a shallow boundary, and a full clone (CI uses fetch-depth: 0) may contain them. No file in tools/gates or tools/agents mentions 'shallow'. (2) Consequence for write-once: r21-shallow-writeonce.mjs (log 05). In clone A, commit M rewrites the write-once round-20/qa-verifier.findings.json (F-DG0-242 High -> Low) and findings.json to match, then commit N follows. checkWriteOnce(A) reports 2 errors ('M event', '2 different contents'). In B = git clone --depth 2 file://A, checkWriteOnce(B) reports 0 errors, and no output says the repository is shallow. The same applies today to every write-once file changed before e8361b8 in every local validation (prefreeze, the qa dry-run, the auditor's clone). (3) Consequence for D-037: in a complete clone, every ancestor of the present gate/round source_commit is present, so an ABSENT fix_revision is provably not in that candidate. The tolerance at rules.mjs:696-698 then accepts exactly the failing case. The unit test 'D-037 / F-DG0-242' even accepts fix_revision '0'x40 for a closure verified in the gate round. The census (log 04, P1) finds 3 closures (F-DG0-226/227/228) whose verifying round-13 source_commit is present while the fix is absent, which is possible only because of the shallow boundary.
findings.expected: The validator detects a shallow repository (git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository). It reports this, and either refuses or runs history checks only when a documented shallow boundary is explicitly allowed. Commit-absence tolerances apply only to commits beyond that boundary, or only when the verifying round's own source_commit is also unavailable, never to a closure in the gate round. D-035/D-037 are corrected to say 'outside the shallow boundary' and state what a full-history (CI) run is expected to show.
findings.actual: History-based integrity checks pass or fail depending on clone depth, without any warning. Tolerances meant for 'pruned' commits also accept fabricated SHAs in a complete clone.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: the repo was SHALLOW not pruned (unshallow restored pre-round-12 commits as real ancestors). validateGate now refuses a shallow repository; gate judged against complete history (CI fetch-depth 0). Backup branch deleted so the round-18 orphan 450c756 is uniformly absent.

verification.note: git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository prints false in the working repository and in a --no-local clone. The pruned-era commits are real ancestors of HEAD: all 22 round source_commits except the D-034-orphaned 450c756 are present and ancestors, and 421c922 is an ancestor. On a --depth=1 --no-local clone, validate.mjs --stage DG0 reports the D-038 shallow error (exit 1); on a complete clone it does not. A clone disguised by deleting .git/shallow still fails closed ('write-once: cannot inspect git history'). CI checks out with fetch-depth: 0, so the refusal does not break CI.

findings.title: The D-037 re-point of F-DG0-150/151 to 421c922 leaves a permanent gate error in any clone that carries the backup branch, while a single-branch clone (CI) passes: the gate verdict depends on which refs the clone has
findings.reproduction: F-DG0-150/151 were last verified by code-security in round 18. stages.json round 18 has source_commit 450c756, which exists only on the local, unpushed branch backup/pre-writeonce-repair-565ab3f and is not an ancestor of HEAD (log 12). D-037 re-pointed their fix_revision to 421c922, which is an ancestor of HEAD but NOT of 450c756 (cb76260, the original, is). Running qa's dry-run docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/real-repo-gate-blockers.mjs on a --no-local clone of HEAD (log 10) therefore reports 2 errors that finishing round 21 cannot clear: 'finding F-DG0-150 (Low): fix 421c922233 is not in the verified round-18 candidate (450c756f67)' and the same for F-DG0-151. The harness buckets them as 'PRUNED', but both commits are present. In a --single-branch clone, 450c756 is absent (log 12), so rules.mjs:696 skips the check and the same gate passes. This contradicts D-037's claim that the dry-run is clean of permanent blockers.
findings.expected: A gate's validation result does not depend on which unrelated refs a clone happens to contain, and F-DG0-150/151's metadata is consistent with the round that verified them. For example, their reporter re-verifies them in a round whose candidate contains 421c922. Alternatively, the fix_revision stays cb76260 and the round-18 source commit is preserved on a pushed ref.
findings.actual: Locally, with the backup branch, validateGate fails permanently on F-DG0-150/151. In CI or a single-branch clone it passes. Fail-closed locally, so no false approval, but the gate cannot pass on this repository as it stands.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: F-DG0-150/151 re-verified in round 22 against the current candidate (fix 421c922, ancestor of HEAD) so their closure is clone-independent; backup branch deleted removes 450c756's conditional presence.

verification.note: No ref contains 450c756 any more (the backup/ branch is gone). It survives only as a reflog-held unreachable object in the working repository. The real-repo dry-run on a --no-local clone reports 0 in the PRUNED, RECORD-LESS and DROPPED buckets. Before this round's re-verification, a local clone that still holds 450c756 reports 2 extra errors for F-DG0-150/151 (dryrun-clone-modes.log). With the round-22 re-verification in place, both clone modes give 0 (f161-reverify-sim.log), so the verdict no longer depends on refs. This closure depends on the F-DG0-150/151 entries in this same sidecar being imported. The general object-store-vs-reachability issue is part of F-DG0-164.

findings.title: Residual 7 still frames the /proc/sys write as a file-tool path, but the agent's Bash shell can open DAC-writable host-global /proc/sys entries for write directly; the new comment's '(userns default)' names the wrong mechanism
findings.reproduction: Probes open(O_WRONLY) and close without writing, so no tunable was changed (logs 13 and 14). From the agent shell (uid 0, NoNewPrivs 1, in its own PID namespace), /proc/sys/vm/swappiness, kernel/shmmax, net/ipv4/ip_forward, vm/drop_caches and kernel/panic all open for write. docs/delivery/threat-model.md:60 (residual 7) describes the exposure as a file tool writing 'directly or by racing a symlink past the guard', and only withdraws the shell claim as 'unverified'. It is now verified that a plain shell redirect reaches these entries, with no race needed. The impact class is unchanged: host availability / kernel tunables, not repository or gate integrity. The /proc/sysrq-trigger vector does not exist on this kernel. Separately, tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py:153 says candidate code in the reviewer's fresh-procfs sandboxes sees /proc/sys read-only '(userns default)'. That holds for tools/gates/sandbox-run.sh only because of its explicit '--ro-bind /proc/sys /proc/sys' (log 13: EROFS). A plain nested 'bwrap --unshare-user --proc /proc' leaves /proc/sys writable.
findings.expected: Residual 7 states that the agent shell, as well as the file tools, can write uid-0 DAC-writable /proc/sys entries directly. The comment attributes the read-only /proc/sys in sandbox-run.sh to its explicit --ro-bind.
findings.actual: The residual understates the vector (shell, no race needed), though not the impact. The comment names the wrong mechanism. I would accept this as an observation: the disclosed impact scope (host-global availability, no integrity effect) is accurate, and F-DG0-149 already carries it.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: residual 7 now states the agent Bash shell (not only file tools) writes host-global /proc/sys directly (verified, no race); comment attributes read-only /proc/sys to sandbox-run.sh's explicit --ro-bind, not a userns default.

verification.note: Wording verified against behaviour. The agent shell opens /proc/sys/vm/swappiness, kernel/shmmax, net/ipv4/ip_forward, kernel/panic and vm/drop_caches for write (open(O_WRONLY)+close only; nothing written). Inside tools/gates/sandbox-run.sh the same entries are 'Read-only file system', because of its explicit '--ro-bind /proc/sys /proc/sys' (sandbox-run.sh:36). Residual 7's body and the agent_sandbox.py comment (lines 149-155) now state exactly this. Cosmetic nit: residual 7's bold heading still reads 'file-tool writes to uid-0-writable /proc/sys entries', while the body correctly covers the shell.

findings.title: Schema subset validator: additionalProperties:false does not reject keys named after Object.prototype members (constructor, toString, __proto__, hasOwnProperty)
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/schema.mjs:59 looks up props[key] on a plain object literal, so props['constructor'] resolves to Object.prototype.constructor, which is truthy. The value is then 'validated' against a keyword-less function and accepted, and the additionalProperties:false branch is never reached. With schema {properties:{a:string}, additionalProperties:false}, validate() reports 'zzz' as unexpected but accepts 'constructor', 'toString', '__proto__' and 'hasOwnProperty' (r21-schema-proto-keys.mjs, log 17). The gate rules read only named fields, so an extra key of this kind cannot change a verdict today.
findings.expected: Use Object.hasOwn(props, key) (and Object.hasOwn(value, key) for required), so every unexpected key is reported.
findings.actual: Prototype-named extra keys pass records, findings and gate schemas silently. I would accept this as an observation: no rule reads such keys.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: schema.mjs uses Object.hasOwn(props,key) and Object.hasOwn(value,key), so extra keys named after Object.prototype members (constructor/toString/__proto__/hasOwnProperty) are rejected by additionalProperties:false. Test D-038/F-DG0-163.

verification.note: schema.mjs uses Object.hasOwn for both required and properties. SEC22-7: additionalProperties:false now rejects constructor, toString, hasOwnProperty, valueOf, __proto__ (own key via JSON.parse), __defineGetter__ and isPrototypeOf, and a required 'constructor' is reported missing when absent. Unit test 'D-038 / F-DG0-163' passes.

findings.title: The D-037 absent-commit tolerance (commitPresent) is not scoped to genuinely pruned commits. checkInvocation now accepts a GATE-round review or audit run whose meta.head_commit_at_start is missing, null, the runner's own fallback 'unknown', or any non-existent 40-hex id. This reopens the round-9 QA5-N52/N53 controls (F-DG0-212 binding: the run must start from a commit that contains the frozen manifest). checkClosure likewise accepts a non-existent (typo'd or all-zero) fix_revision on a closure verified in a round whose own source_commit is present, including the gate round.
findings.reproduction: QA_REPO_ROOT=<fresh clone of a0e077d> node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r21.test.mjs (log docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-21/11-qa21-negative-tests.log). On the independent fully-evidenced fixture (0 errors as control, QA21-G0), for each of domain-reviewer, code-security-reviewer, qa-verifier and release-auditor in the gate round, rewrite the run's meta.json: QA21-C4 head_commit_at_start = 'f'x40, QA21-C5 field deleted, QA21-C5b null, QA21-C5d 'unknown' (tools/agents/run-agent.sh:64 writes exactly this when `git rev-parse HEAD` fails). validateGate(current) returns 0 errors in all 16 cases (ACCEPTED). The round-9 suite re-run under round-21 rules (log round-21/10-r20-suite-rerun.log, QA20-G1) now fails QA5-N52 and QA5-N53, which passed through round 20. QA21-C3: a closure verified in the gate round (round-2, source_commit present) with fix_revision = the real fix with its last hex digit changed, or '0'x40, gives 0 errors. In a full clone a missing commit can never be an ancestor of a present one, so this is provably not 'in the candidate'. The existing unit test 'D-037 / F-DG0-242' (validator.test.mjs line ~1115) codifies the all-zero case in the gate round as accepted. Root cause: rules.mjs checkInvocation calls `if (commitPresent(repo, meta.head_commit_at_start)) {...}` and checkClosure calls `commitPresent(fix) && commitPresent(round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(...)`. Any value that does not resolve, whatever its shape and whichever round it is in, is treated as 'pruned'. Controls: a PRESENT fix that is not in the candidate is still rejected (QA21-C1 descendant, QA21-C2 dangling), and the real-repo dry-run is clean (round-21/13-real-repo-gate-blockers.log).
findings.expected: D-037 states that the tolerance covers commits 'pruned by a later legitimate history correction (the pre-round-12 truncation, the D-034 rewrite)', and that 'a run that started before the manifest is still caught'. By the same reasoning as D-036/F-DG0-240 (the D-035 tolerance must not reach the gate's own round), the tolerance should apply only to (a) a well-formed ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ value, never to a missing, null, 'unknown' or other malformed head_commit_at_start (those were rejected before D-037), and (b) a round that is itself pruned, i.e. whose source_commit is also absent, and never to the gate round. This is feasible on the real history: every one of the 33 record runs with an absent head_commit_at_start belongs to rounds 1-12, whose source_commits are all absent, and all 61 verifier runs with an absent head belong to pruned rounds. For closures, only F-DG0-226/227/228 (verified in round 13, present, fix d1352f4 absent) would need their fix_revision re-pointed at a retained commit that contains the fix, as was done for F-DG0-150/151. Add unit tests for the checkInvocation tolerance; D-037 added one only for checkClosure.
findings.actual: The tolerance is a blanket skip for any unresolvable value in any round, including the gate round. Exploiting it needs a run meta.json written without (or with a bogus) head commit before the runner commits it, or a history rewrite, because runs/** is write-once after commit, i.e. the orchestrator-level actor of threat-model residual 1. An honest runner fault ('unknown') would also pass silently. Other run bindings (assignment sha, started_at >= frozen_at, transcript replay, outputs) still hold. Fail-open on a mechanically enforced control that passed in round 20, so Medium, not mandatory. findings.title: agent_sandbox.py finish(): when one of the role's own new review files already exists in the real directory (another run of the same role and round committed it after this run's prepare), copy-back crashes with an uncaught FileExistsError. It leaves a partial copy-back (files sorted before the collision are already in the real tree) and writes no sandbox.json, contrary to the threat model's statement that discarded writes are listed in sandbox.json
findings.reproduction: Disposable fixture under $TMPDIR (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-17/12-copyback-collision-probe.log, script included). `agent_sandbox.py prepare qa-verifier ...`, then in the staging copy write round-2/qa-verifier.findings.json and round-2/qa-verifier.json. Then create round-2/qa-verifier.json in the REAL reviews dir (a concurrent run of the same role committing first). `agent_sandbox.py finish <state> <out>` exits 1 with 'FileExistsError: [Errno 17] File exists: .../round-2/qa-verifier.json' (the O_EXCL open). The real round-2 now holds THIS run's qa-verifier.findings.json next to the OTHER run's qa-verifier.json, and <out>/sandbox.json is not written. The real record is not overwritten (QA17-S4 passes on that point).
findings.expected: A collision on the role's own new file is handled like the other refusals: nothing is copied for that file, the collision is listed in sandbox.json 'discarded' (for example 'exists in the real tree (written concurrently); not copied'), finish() exits 3, and ideally no file of the run is copied back at all when any of them collides (check first, then copy), so the real tree never holds a mixed record/sidecar pair.
findings.actual: Fail-closed only. run-agent.sh treats any non-zero finish as SANDBOX_RC and a review run then exits 73 without auto-committing, the real record is preserved (O_EXCL), and a mixed pair would not bind to one run's transcript under D-021. It needs two concurrent runs of the same role for the same round, which the orchestrator does not schedule. But the evidence the threat model promises (sandbox.json with the discard list, meta.process_sandbox_*) is missing for that run, and an uncommitted foreign sidecar is left in the real reviews directory for the orchestrator to notice. Low and non-mandatory. I would accept it as an observation for DG0.

findings.title: D-038 scoping is keyed on a forgeable, object-store-based 'round absent' test: a superseded round whose frozen manifest records a non-existent source_commit re-opens the absent-fix tolerance, so a CLOSED_VERIFIED finding passes with an all-zero or typo'd fix_revision and the gate-candidate ancestry check is skipped
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:725-733 (checkClosure) sets roundAbsent = !commitPresent(round.source_commit), and when the fix_revision is also absent it pushes no error. The gate check at :731 sits only in the fix-PRESENT branch. round.source_commit is metadata: checkReviewRounds (:749) only requires it to equal the round's committed manifest.source_commit, and findManifest (:903-909) tolerates a manifest whose source_commit does not exist. Nothing requires a non-gate round's source_commit to exist or to be an ancestor of the commit that froze its manifest. Reproduction on the validator's own fixture (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-22/sec22-repro.tests.mjs.txt, run by run-sec22-repro.sh on a --no-local clone of 7cf94db; log sec22-repro.log): round 2 verifies F-DG0-101 (High, mandatory); round 3 is the gate round. The round-2 manifest is committed with source_commit 'deadbeef'x5, and real round-2 runs start from the commit that contains it. SEC22-1 (real fix): 0 errors. SEC22-2 (fix_revision = 0x40): 0 errors. SEC22-3 (fix_revision = one-character typo of the real fix): 0 errors. SEC22-4 control: a PRESENT off-branch fix is still caught ('is not in the gate candidate'). Retained and gate rounds hold (SEC22-5: unknown/HEAD/missing/null/zeros/uppercase/short heads and zero/f fix_revisions are all rejected). The same predicate gates checkInvocation's head tolerance (:399/:408), so in such a round a fabricated 40-hex head_commit_at_start is also accepted. Second symptom of the same root cause: commitPresent (:595-602) tests object-store membership, not reachability. The working repository still holds round 18's 450c756 through its reflog, while a --no-local clone does not, so validateGate(current) on the same commit differs by 2 errors (F-DG0-150/151 'fix 421c922 is not in the verified round-18 candidate') between the two clone modes (dryrun-clone-modes.mjs/.log). Why the tolerance has no remaining legitimate use: the validator now refuses shallow clones (F-DG0-160), and in a complete clone every ancestor of the gate source_commit is present. An absent fix_revision is therefore provably NOT in the gate candidate. Census on a --no-local clone (tolerance-census.log): 0 findings have an absent fix_revision; the only absent round is 18; and the only closures whose verifying run has an absent head are F-DG0-150/151, which this round re-verifies in round 22 (f161-reverify-sim.log: afterwards 0 dependent errors in both clone modes).
findings.expected: D-038 states the tolerance is 'never a retained round'. Retained-ness must not be something a single metadata value can declare. After this round nothing needs the absent-fix tolerance, so: (1) in checkClosure, reject any CLOSED_VERIFIED fix_revision that is not present AND an ancestor of the gate source_commit (and of the verifying round's source_commit when present), with no round-absent escape; (2) in checkInvocation, either drop the absent-head tolerance or restrict it to an explicit, reviewed allowlist of orphaned rounds (round 18, D-034); (3) decide 'absent' deterministically, e.g. by 'not an ancestor of HEAD' rather than by object-store membership, so unreachable reflog objects cannot change a verdict; (4) optionally, for a non-gate round whose manifest source_commit is present, require it to be an ancestor of the commit that introduced the manifest. Add fixture tests for SEC22-2/3.

findings.title: Findings sidecars in non-gate rounds are not bound to any run, and the latest raising sidecar supersedes the reviewer's immutable fields, so an added later-round sidecar can silently downgrade a finding's severity and mandatory_violation
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:495 keeps only the LATEST sidecar version of each finding ('later rounds supersede earlier versions'), and :537-539 compares findings.json's IMMUTABLE_FINDING_FIELDS (stage_id, requirement, severity, mandatory_violation, title, reported_by) against that version only. A <role>.findings.json is bound to a run's tool-authored outputs only for the gate-round records (checkReview :463). checkClosure binds only the verifications sidecar (:714), and checkReviewRounds (:752-763) only checks that a listed record's sidecar exists. write-once (:781) forbids modifying committed files, not adding new ones. Reproduction (sec22-repro.tests.mjs.txt SEC22-8, log sec22-repro.log): genuine 3-round fixture, with F-DG0-101 raised High/mandatory in round 1, verified in round 2, gate round 3; control 0 errors. With no reviewer run, add docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-2/code-security-reviewer.findings.json re-listing F-DG0-101 as Low / mandatory_violation false, and set the same values in findings.json: 0 errors. Negative control: the same findings.json downgrade WITHOUT the added sidecar is caught ('severity in findings.json ("Low") differs from the reviewer's ("High")').
findings.expected: A reviewer's classification of a finding can change only through a sidecar that the reviewer's own run demonstrably wrote. Either bind every findings sidecar (any round) to its role's run for that round, i.e. require it to be among that run's tool-authored outputs, as checkReview does for the gate round; or compare the immutable fields against EVERY raising sidecar version (or the earliest), so a later version cannot differ.
findings.actual: An added, unbound findings sidecar in any non-gate round later than the raising round re-classifies a High/mandatory finding as Low/non-mandatory without a validator error. Closing it still needs bound reviewer and auditor runs (for example ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION, which is only allowed for Low non-mandatory findings), so the effect is a misrepresented finding presented to those reviewers, not a direct gate pass. Hence Low.

findings.title: The commitPresent() header comment in tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs still says checkClosure and checkInvocation tolerate an absent commit (D-037), which D-039 removed
findings.reproduction: In a --no-local clone at 6438e20, `sed -n 596,601p tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs` reads: 'Provenance checks that need such a commit tolerate its genuine absence (D-035 for findManifest; D-037 for checkClosure and checkInvocation), while every check whose commit IS present still runs'. `grep -n commitPresent tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs` shows its only callers are checkInvocation (line 397), which rejects an absent head, and checkClosure (lines 731 and 733). Line 731 rejects an absent fix. Line 733 skips only the round-ancestry test when the round's source_commit is absent, and the gate-ancestry test still runs. The in-function comments at lines 390 and 723-729 and decisions.md D-039 correctly say there is no absent-commit escape (19-stale-commitPresent-comment.log).
findings.expected: After D-039, the header comment should say that the only absence tolerance is findManifest's content-preserving one (D-035), plus the skipped round-ancestry test when a round's source_commit is absent. It should not describe checkClosure/checkInvocation as tolerating an absent fix or head.
findings.actual: The comment describes the removed D-037 behaviour. Behaviour is correct and strict (the unit tests 'D-039 / F-DG0-164/246' and 'D-039 / F-DG0-164' pass, see 18-d039-tests.log). The inaccuracy is in a code comment only and makes no business, operating-logic or source-provenance claim. It could mislead a future maintainer or reviewer about what the validator tolerates, the same class of wording issue as F-DG0-013. I would accept it as a Low observation or as a one-line comment fix in the next stage.

history.note: raised by domain-reviewer in DG0 round 23 (Low, non-mandatory; comment-only inaccuracy, behaviour correct; acceptable as an observation)

findings.title: checkClosure still skips the 'fix is in the verified round candidate' check when the verifying round's source_commit is absent, a predicate that forged round metadata alone can satisfy. A PRESENT fix committed after the verifier's run started (so absent from both the round candidate and the run's head) still closes the finding
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:733 runs `if (commitPresent(repo, round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(fix, round.source_commit))`. round.source_commit is orchestrator metadata that checkReviewRounds (:752) only requires to equal the round manifest's source_commit, and findManifest (:895-913) tolerates a manifest whose source_commit does not exist. SEC23-7 in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-23/sec23-repro.tests.mjs.txt (run by run-sec23-repro.sh on a --no-local clone of 6438e20; log sec23-repro.log) sets up round 2 to verify F-DG0-101 (High, mandatory) and round 3 as the gate round on a new candidate. The fix commit is a content change committed AFTER round 2's runs started, so it is not an ancestor of the round-2 verifier's head_commit_at_start (fix-in-verifier-head=false). Control, round 2 genuine (source_commit present): 1 error, 'fix … is not in the verified round-2 candidate'. Forged, round 2's committed manifest and stages entry name source_commit 'deadbeef'x5, entries self-consistent: 0 errors. D-039 closed the ABSENT-fix variant (SEC23-2/3: all-zero and typo'd fixes are rejected), and the fix must still be an ancestor of the gate candidate (SEC23-4). What remains is only the round-level binding: the reviewer's PASS is recorded as verifying a fix its run could not have seen. Real-repo census (tolerance-census.log): the only absent round is 18, and no CLOSED_VERIFIED closure is verified in round 18. So the skipped branch has no legitimate use today and is reachable only through forged round metadata. Exploitation still needs a genuine reviewer PASS verification in the forged round, so the effect is a mis-attributed fix_revision, not an unfixed finding in the gate candidate.
findings.expected: A CLOSED_VERIFIED closure must be tied to content the verifying run could actually see, whatever the round metadata says. Two options: (a) additionally require isAncestor(fix_revision, meta.head_commit_at_start) of the verifying run (always present and 40-hex after D-039, and a descendant of the round's source_commit in every legitimate case); or (b) reject a CLOSED_VERIFIED closure verified in a round whose source_commit is absent (no current closure depends on one). Optionally also require head_commit_at_start to be reachable from HEAD (isAncestor(head, HEAD)), not merely present in the object store, so an unreachable local object cannot change a verdict between clone modes (fail-closed in CI today). Add a fixture test like SEC23-7.
findings.actual: With a forged absent round source_commit, a present fix that is in the gate candidate but not in the verified round's candidate, nor in the verifier's run head, passes validateGate with 0 errors. The same fixture with a genuine round reports the error.

findings.title: Stale comment: rules.mjs:597-601 (commitPresent) still says checkClosure and checkInvocation tolerate a commit's genuine absence (D-037). D-039 removed those tolerances

findings.title: checkClosure still skips the verified-round ancestry check when the round's source_commit is (self-declared) absent. A present fix that is in the gate candidate but NOT in the verifying run's starting history closes a finding. D-039 now requires head_commit_at_start to be present, so the head could bind the fix instead.
findings.reproduction: QA_REPO_ROOT=<complete clone of the candidate> node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r23.test.mjs, case QA23-P1 (log docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-23/13-qa23-negative-suite.log). Start from the independent fixture, which validates with 0 errors (QA23-G0). (1) Commit a round-3 manifest whose entries hash correctly to its candidate_id and whose source_commit = 'ab' x 20 (never existed). Add a matching stages.json round-3 entry. (2) The qa-verifier round-3 run's head_commit_at_start is a PRESENT commit that contains that manifest but does not have the fix in its history (the fixture uses a parentless commit on a kept branch; on a linear history this is any fix committed after the run started). (3) The run's sidecar closes F-DG0-201 (High). The mirror sets fix_revision = a real commit that IS an ancestor of the gate candidate. validateGate = [] (ACCEPTED). Root cause: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs checkClosure `if (commitPresent(repo, round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(repo, f.fix_revision, round.source_commit))` skips the round binding when round.source_commit is absent. That is a corollary of findManifest's D-035 tolerance and is documented in D-039 ('when its source_commit resolves'). The fix is not compared with the verifying run's head_commit_at_start, which D-039 now requires to be present.
findings.expected: A CLOSED_VERIFIED fix_revision is bound to content the verifier could have seen, whatever the round metadata says. Proposal: in checkClosure, also require isAncestor(fix_revision, <verifying run's head_commit_at_start>), or use that as the fallback when round.source_commit is absent. The head is now always present and must contain the round manifest, and on a genuine history fix <= source_commit <= freeze/manifest commit <= head. Feasibility on the real history: all 104 CLOSED_VERIFIED fixes are already ancestors of their verifying run's head, and none is verified in a round whose source_commit is absent (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-23/21-fix-revision-integrity-nl.log). So the stricter rule costs nothing today. Add a unit test for the QA23-P1 shape.
findings.actual: validateGate returns 0 errors for QA23-P1. Scope is narrower than F-DG0-246, which this round verifies as fixed: the fix must be a real, present commit in the gate candidate (QA23-N1/N2/N4 show absent, all-zero and off-branch fixes are rejected), and the closure still comes from a genuine reviewer sidecar. Only the binding between the verifying run and the named fix commit depends on orchestrator-written round metadata. No real closure is affected (0 on the full history).
